record_type_quote: To further investigate the biological significance of this result, we attempted to reproduce this phenomenon in an independent laboratory using different genotypes and additional mating assays.

targets.authors: Sharon G, Segal D, Ringo JM, Hefetz A, Zilber-Rosenberg I, Rosenberg E.
targets.title: Commensal bacteria play a role in mating preference of Drosophila melanogaster.
targets.evidence_quote: We used a four-fly mate choice design to replicate the methods of Sharon et al. (2010) .
targets.outcome_quote: In partial replication of this previous result, we found that flies from the Canton-S strain mate assortatively based on the diets of their ancestors. Though we did not explicitly investigate the presence of any particular bacterial species, this is consistent with the pattern observed by Sharon et al. (2010) with the Oregon-R strain. In contrast, we saw random mating in flies from our outbred allRAL strain.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly describe partial replication and contrast agreement in the inbred strain with random mating in the outbred strain.

reasoning: New fly populations test the published ancestral-diet assortative mating finding. The correction is not a separate target; other cited assortative-mating work supplies background.
